title: Fluffy American pancakes
intro: Tall and fluffy, with maple syrup and berries: the Sunday breakfast.

steps.t: In a bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
In another, whisk milk, eggs and the slightly cooled melted butter.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir just briefly with a fork: a few lumps are fine. Let the batter rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and grease it lightly with butter. Pour a small ladle (60 ml) of batter per pancake.
Cook until bubbles appear on top and the edges look dry, then flip and cook until golden.
steps.label: Pancakes

steps.t: Serve in stacks with maple syrup and berries.

tips.t: Don't overmix: lumps make fluffy pancakes, a smooth batter makes rubbery ones.
Use buttermilk instead of milk (or milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice) for even taller pancakes.
Leftovers freeze well: reheat them straight in the toaster.

title: Vegan apple cinnamon porridge
intro: Creamy oats with warm cinnamon apples and toasted walnuts.

steps.t: Dice the apple and cook it in a small pan with half the syrup, the cinnamon and a splash of water until soft.
steps.label: Apples

steps.t: Meanwhile, put the oats, oat milk, water and salt in another pan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring.

microwave.t: Meanwhile, put the oats, oat milk, water and salt in a large microwave-safe bowl.

steps.t: Cook on low heat, stirring often, until the porridge is thick and creamy.
steps.label: Porridge

microwave.t: Microwave at 800 W, stirring every minute, until thick and creamy.

steps.t: Spoon into bowls and top with the apples, broken walnuts and the rest of the syrup.

tips.t: The pinch of salt isn't a mistake: it's what makes porridge taste sweeter and fuller.
In autumn try pears and ginger; in winter banana and a spoonful of peanut butter.

title: French toast
intro: Day-old brioche soaked in milk and egg and fried golden in butter: nothing goes to waste.

steps.t: Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Soak the slices about 20 seconds per side, until well soaked but not falling apart.
Melt half the butter in a pan over medium heat until foaming.
Cook the slices, adding the rest of the butter when you flip them, until golden outside and set inside.
steps.label: Pan

steps.t: Serve hot with berries and a dusting of powdered sugar.

tips.t: Use bread at least a day old: fresh bread soaks up too much and falls apart.
Savory twist: skip the sugar, sandwich a slice of cheese between two slices and add salt.

title: Coconut mango chia pudding
intro: Chia seeds set in coconut milk, layered with mango and toasted coconut.

steps.t: In a bowl or jar, stir together chia, coconut drink, maple syrup and vanilla really well.
Leave it to rest, then stir again to break up any clumps.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Cover and chill until thick and spoonable (overnight is fine).
steps.label: Fridge

steps.t: Blend half the mango with a squeeze of lime and dice the rest. Toast the coconut in a dry pan.
Layer pudding, mango purée and diced mango in glasses and finish with toasted coconut and lime zest.

tips.t: Stir again after 10 minutes: that's what stops the seeds clumping at the bottom.
The plain pudding keeps 4 days in the fridge: make double and add the fruit just before eating.

title: Crunchy homemade granola
intro: Oats, almonds and seeds toasted with maple syrup: crunchy, in big clusters.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160 °C and line a large tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, mix oats, roughly chopped almonds, pumpkin seeds, coconut, cinnamon and salt.
Gently warm the syrup, oil and vanilla, pour over the dry mix and stir until everything is coated.
Spread on the tray in an even layer and press down with the back of a spoon: that's what makes clusters.
Bake, turning the tray halfway but without stirring, until golden and fragrant.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool completely on the tray: it crisps up as it cools.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Break into clusters, add the raisins and store in an airtight jar.

tips.t: Add the dried fruit only after baking: in the oven it would burn and go hard.
Great with Greek or plant yogurt and seasonal fruit, or simply with cold milk.
In an airtight jar it stays crunchy for 3 weeks.
